ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher; no account flag is warranted on this no-show claim
ruling.reasoning:
NS-0 routes this case: the trip was cancelled by the driver [F4] on a driver-side no-show claim, so the $6.61 fee stands only through NS-1. The trace settles the first two conditions: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 13:02:35 [F6] and was 39 m from the pickup at that moment [F6][F1], so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are met — the rider advocate rightly conceded this [F6].

Condition NS-1 (iii) fails on the records. After the 13:02:35 tap the driver stayed continuously within 200 m of the pickup for only 2 min 55 s (175 s), and cancelled at 13:05:30 [F6][F4]; the required continuous wait is more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01, threshold 180 s), so the element is not satisfied [F6]. The driver advocate's answer is to measure from the earlier platform arrival at 13:01:00 (4 min 30 s before cancellation) [F2][F5], but NS-1 (iii) counts only waiting after the arrival confirmation, and the record itself ties the confirmation to the 13:02:35 tap [F6]; the pre-tap presence in the vicinity is expressly excluded [F2][F6]. The stationary window of 3 min 15 s at 40 m [F3] also begins at 13:02:15, 20 s before the tap [F6], and does not cure the shortfall.

The driver's own contemporaneous message is consistent with the records rather than curing them: at 13:05 he declared "More than 3 min already, I have to cancel" [F10], yet the tap he relies on was at 13:02:35 [F6] — a driver's assertion of elapsed time is not a system record, and system records override statements [F12][F10][F6]. The chat is complete and fully timestamped but contains no rider message at all [F9][F10][F11], so neither side's account of when the rider emerged is settled by the record; that timing is not needed here because the fee already fails on NS-1 (iii) [F6].

With (iii) unmet, NS-2 applies: the $6.61 is refunded in full [F7][F4]. The published-fee and surge points [F7][F8] do not make the fee payable, since NS-0 lets it stand only through the NS-1 conditions.

No account flag: the flag condition in NS-2 (arrival confirmed while not at the pickup) is not met — the tap was inside the radius [F6][F1] — and RD-6 is not engaged because RD-2 refunds nothing on a no-show fee; the $6.61 is not a route-deviation refund. Profile facts (the driver's 1 upheld no-show in 90 days [F17], the rider's clean record [F16]) cannot decide the case and do not create an account action here.

Safety screen: I read every message, the driver's statement and the complaint [F9][F10][F12][F11]; the messages concern the pickup, the wait and the cancellation only, and nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is "none". Evidence is sufficient: the trace shows the GPS track runs from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation without a gap, and the arrival tap, tap-time distance and post-tap duration are all recorded [F2][F3][F5][F6].

Amount: the fee on record is a flat $6.61 no-show cancellation fee [F7][F4], refunded in full under NS-2, so the refund is $6.61 (voucher form per NS-7).

rejected_claims.reason: F2/F5 show the driver within 200 m from 13:01:00, but NS-1 (iii) counts continuous waiting only after the arrival confirmation, which the record places at the 13:02:35 tap [F6]; pre-tap presence in the vicinity does not satisfy it.
The 3 min 15 s stationary window starts at 13:02:15 [F3], 20 s before the 13:02:35 tap [F6]; the post-tap interval inside the radius is only 2 min 55 s, below the > 3 min requirement of NS-1 (iii).
Measured from the tap at 13:02:35 [F6] to the 13:05:30 cancellation [F4] is 2 min 55 s, which is short of ≥ 3:01; the claim states its own refutation.
The chat is complete and timestamped [F9][F10][F11] but contains no rider message; the driver's assertion of elapsed time [F10] is not a system record and does not satisfy NS-1 (iii) [F6].
That $6.61 was the published fee with surge 1.0× [F7][F8] does not make it payable; NS-0 lets the fee stand only through the NS-1 conditions, and (iii) fails [F6], so NS-2 requires full refund.

The claim that the fee was validly incurred after a > 3 min post-tap wait is contradicted by F6; the rider's own account of emerging is unsettled by the record [F9][F10][F11], so neither statement supports the fee.
NS-1 (iii) is not met — 175 s post-tap versus the > 180 s requirement [F6] — so NS-2, not no_action, applies.

The legal conclusion is correct (fee fails under NS-1 (iii) [F6]), but the rider advocate's framing of C1 as the operative grievance is accepted; no part of C1 is rejected as to outcome — retained here only to record that its factual premise rests on the same F6 the ruling adopts.
Profile facts (rider clean record [F16], driver's 1 upheld no-show [F17]) cannot decide the case and do not support an account-review action on this claim; RD-6 is not engaged on a no-show fee.
